sentences.text: The known remains include parts of the skull, the lower jaw, several vertebrae, ribs, and a hind fin.
Its braincase is very primitive and looks more like other diapsids than other ichthyosaurs.
The rear appendage is extremely long and thin, built with stretched-out thigh, shin, and ankle bones.
Each spinal bone has two matching hollow spaces at the front, likely helping the animal float.
The skull is mostly broken apart, though specific bones like the quadratojugal and postorbital are preserved.
The lower jaw measures about 40 centimeters in length and holds many cone-shaped teeth for spearing fish.
A specific bone process on the skull is found in this species and only one other known ichthyosaur.
The animal kept postparietal bones, a primitive trait missing in all other known ichthyosaurs.
Remains were found in 1965, but the species was not formally named until 1997 by Sander.
However, the genus name was actually coined earlier by Maisch and Matzke in the year 2000.
Only a single fossil occurrence of this animal has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
The limb structure suggests the creature was long but not particularly powerful, generating a reasonable amount of lift.
Phantomosaurus belongs to the parent group Cymbospondylidae.
It is classified within the family Cymbospondylidae.
The animal is classified as a reptile.
The shape of the quadratojugal bone is very similar to those of other large cymbospondylid ichthyosaurs.
Fossils of this animal have been found in southern Germany.
